text: 65-year-old male. The patient complains of persistent fatigue and reports poor sleep quality. He mentions adopting a vegetarian diet in recent months to improve his energy levels but hasn't noticed significant benefits. The patient reports losing weight without trying over the last month.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancreatic Cancer

The combination of a significantly enlarged, thin-walled gallbladder (Courvoisier's sign), obstructive jaundice, and unexplained weight loss in a 65-year-old male is highly characteristic of a malignancy obstructing the common bile duct. Given the absence of stones and the specific ultrasound findings, a mass in the head of the pancreas is the leading etiology.
